newsitem.title: CONGO: Congo president praises new tolerance.
newsitem.headline: Congo president praises new tolerance.

text.p: Congo's President Pascal Lissouba, who faces polls in July, praised a new spirit of tolerance in the Central African nation since the bloody ethnic and political clashes in 1993.

But Lissouba, in a broadcast New Year address to the nation late on Tuesday, expressed concern about delays in the gathering in of weapons distributed at the time of the unrest, which followed multi-party parliamentary elections.
Earlier, he denounced a clan mentality and a mercenary attitude and corruption among certain elements in the army.
Addressing soldiers, he called for "professionalism" in the run-up to the presidential elections in July.
Congo and other African nations embarked on a process of democratic reform after the collapse of Communism in the Soviet bloc at the end of the 1980s.

Ethnic violence unleashed by disputed parliamentary elections in 1993 degenerated into clashes among rival party militias, killing an estimated 2,000 people in the southern suburbs of the former French colony's capital Brazzaville.
